Mountain hikes Schleier Waterfall circular hiking route

Going am Wilden Kaiser / Kaiser Mountains
Difficulty ratings: medium
Route length: 5.5 km
Duration: 3:00 h

The veil waterfall of Going, with its sometimes delicate, sometimes dense silver water, is a place of power with a special spirit. From beautiful vantage points, you can even see its veil from behind!

Tour character

The Schleier Waterfall is the highlight of several hikes with different levels of difficulty. Sure-footedness is required for all of them. No problem for climbers who head for the climbing paradise at the waterfall. The Schleierwasserfall loop is particularly beautiful: a moderately difficult hike of 5.5 kilometers over alpine pastures, forest paths and narrow mountain trails. It starts at the Hüttling parking lot in Going and also passes the Stiegenbach Falls.

Trail condition

The composition of the trail varies between forest roads, meadow paths, forest trails and short sections of asphalt.

Equipment

Rucksack, hiking/mountaineering boots, hiking gear (breathable), sun protection (sunglasses, sun cream, headgear), waterproofs (hardshell), water bottle, food for eating on the way, hiking poles if desired, plastic bag for waste, hiking map
Source: TVB Wilder Kaiser

Description

This tour starts at the Hüttling hiking start point.
 
Give yourself some time here and have a look at the small chapel, also from inside, and fill your water bottle with fresh Kaiser water from the fountain next door.
 
The forest road now takes you towards the Wilder Kaiser. When you come to the “Fußweg-Wasserfall-Graspoint” intersection, the trail leads you across Alpine pastures and through the forest and, after about 20 minutes, you continue on the forest road.
 
A narrow path, which requires a certain degree of surefootedness, now brings you to the Schleier Waterfall, a paradise for climbers. Here at this power place of Going, the waterfall trickles down over the overhanging rock faces, creating a magnificent natural stage set. This is the perfect place for your holiday photo. But also the climbers feel very much at home on the demanding rocks and are constantly looking for new challenges. You might even come across the “Huber Buam” here, a pair of famous extreme climbers.
 
You carry on past the overhanging rocks heading towards the Stiegenbach Waterfall. From there a path takes you through Alpine meadows and forest to the Graspoint-Niederalm (981 m) where you can take a well earned break. (The Graspoint-Niederalm is not staffed, but bottled drinks are available in the well. Please bring small change).
 
Suitably fortified, you then hike downhill along the forest road till you come to the Aschinger-chapel, the starting point of your tour.

Getting here

  • Arrival by public transport

    KaiserJet stop “Going Badesee” or "Going Dorf" or Postbus stop "Going Stanglwirt" or "Going Dorf".
    More information at: www.wilderkaiser.info/mobility

  • Parking

    Heading from St. Johann on the B178 road, take the Going Prama exit immediately after passing the Stanglwirt hotel. When you reach the first junction, turn right in the direction of the bathing lake. Keep following the road towards the Kaisergebirge mountain range until you reach the next junction, which is located between two farmhouses. Turn left here and follow the road until you reach the hiking starting point and the car park.

    Heading from Wörgl or Kufstein on the B178 road, take the Going Prama exit before you reach the Stanglwirt hotel. When you reach the first junction, turn right in the direction of the bathing lake. Keep following the road towards the Kaisergebirge mountain range until you reach the next junction, which is located between two farmhouses. Turn left here and follow the road until you reach the hiking starting point and the car park.
    Hüttling car park, Going (820 m) - pay & display
    It is a day car park, which means that no ticket can be purchased for several days. The parking ticket is therefore only valid on the day of issue! It is a public car park from May to October. During the winter months from November to April the car park is not attended. During this time the use is at your own risk! Camping and permanent parking is prohibited on this car park. (Vehicles that are parked illegally will be reported to the police and towed.)
